doc.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Law school, racism in Toledo and the trip to New York
summary: Denied the probation job because of race, turned back at Canada, and he goes to New York.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: that is not done. But I never paid any attention to those things. I truly never paid attention to any of that stuff. So here I was in this situation where they had sent a guy to my house and he told me he says, “Jon, you’ve got to withdraw your name.” I said, “why? I earned it, are you kidding? I earned that.” He says, “look, if you insist on this, they’re going to lean on me, and you know I’ve got a wife and two kids.” I said, “okay.” So I said hum, that means I’m not going anywhere in Toledo, however brilliant I am, I am going nowhere in that society. That’s the notice they served on me. So I’d been singing at night, I was singing and playing drums, and doing very well at that too. So I says I think I’ll go somewhere where I’ll have more freedom. So I figured maybe I’d go to Canada, that’s the end of the underground railroad, it’s much more liberal there, that’d be a good place for my family. So I went to the Canadian border and they asked me did I have a thousand dollars in cash on me. I said no, I’ve only got three hundred. They said, “well you have to have a thousand if you’re going to immigrate into Canada.” I said, “I don’t have a thousand, I have three hundred.” They said, “well you can’t do it.” So they turned me away at the border. So I figured I’ll go to New York, and that guy Charlie Parker, I’ll look him up. So on the way to Buffalo from the border, my old Chevy broke down. Conked out. So I get a ride into the city, and I just left the car because it was finished. And I got on the Greyhound bus and went into New York. And I got off at the bus station and I remembered Joe Carroll in Toledo was singing with Dizzy, which was my gig, I was supposed to be Dizzy’s first singer. But I had moved from Rochester back to Toledo and he had come to Rochester looking for me and couldn’t find me and hired Joe Carroll. So I called Joe and I said, “where is Bird?” He said, “The Apollo Bar, 125th Street and Seventh Avenue.” I almost dropped the phone. This was two years and four months later. I said whew.
He was right, anybody would know where he is.
